messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: gpuhost-17 observed repeated Xid resets and ECC correctable surge. 4 driver resets in last 2m. Affected service: inference-hosted. Severity: P1. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-xid

maria-nguyen: ack - I'm oncall. looking into it now.

maria-nguyen: quick question - are we seeing pod OOMs or kernel-level panics? any direct customer errors yet?

dave-kim: containers are restarting, kube shows evictions on pods pinned to gpuhost-17. telemetry shows KV cache mem spikes around the same time as Xid. snippet from dmesg:

```
NVRM: Xid (79): GPU has fallen off the bus.
NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x23)
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (87): ECC error corrected, count=42
[  123.789012] kernel: oom-kill: killing process 12345 (inference-worker) total-vm:123456kB, anon-rss:98765kB, file-rss:0kB
```

jen-support: support: we've got two customer reports: increased latency and ~5% failed inferences on /v1/generate for a high-volume tenant started ~2m ago. CS @oncall-schedule alerted.

maria-nguyen: ok cordoning gpuhost-17 now. plan: drain with graceful timeout, route traffic off-node, then attempt driver restart. @dave can you take driver restart and watch logs?

dave-kim: running: `kubectl cordon gpuhost-17 && kubectl drain gpuhost-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m`
I'll run: `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver` then `sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia` if needed.

ops-bot: Telemetry snapshot for gpuhost-17: ECC correctables 120 -> 410 over 3m, Xid resets correlate with 20% spike in kvcache allocation. Suggest quarantine if driver restart doesn't hold.

chao: saw similar last month - temporary mitigation was to lower batch sizes and disable continuous batching on impacted hosts. Recommend toggling routing to fallback pool and enabling batch throttling for heavy tenants.

maria-nguyen: applying routing rule to avoid node:gpuhost-17 (smart-routing) - should propagate in ~30s. will also flip batch throttle for the large tenant.

jen-support: posting interim status on status.redwood: "Investigating GPU instability impacting inference latency for a subset of customers. On-call is mitigating."

dave-kim: driver restart attempted. logs show driver came back but there were two quick Xid followups within 30s. running `nvidia-bug-report.sh` and collecting logs. If resets persist we'll reprovision the GPU and open hardware case.

maria-nguyen: pods moved to fallback pool, initial latency metrics improving. still watching for any new Xid.

ops-bot: update: if resets continue after reprovision, next steps: 1) reprovision host 2) hardware ticket with vendor 3) schedule maintenance window for node replacement.

chao: long-term: consider firmware bump for this GPU family + driver rollback to last-known-good if telemetry suggests driver regression.

maria-nguyen: ack. I'll keep this thread active while we monitor for 30m. tagging oncall-restore if we need swap-out. :white_check_mark:

jen-support: CS continues customer comms; will escalate to enterprise AE if errors persist.

ops-bot: summary: gpuhost-17 cordoned and drained, traffic routed off-node, driver restart attempted, initial improvement observed, telemetry still elevated. Next check-in in 10m.
